My comments are not meant to detract or conflict with other approaches mentioned in this thread. My suggestions are ways/systems I have been involved with that have worked for me and others. We do have our water tested by independent, state certified labs.

There are many variations you could pursue with varying results. Be safe; think through the ramifications of altering your water supply and water supply system. There are invariably unintended consequences with utilizing any water treatment system.

Whole house (filtering bad stuff out of municipal water supply)-

Stage 1- 4 1/2" x 20" Aquaboon pleated (rinse able) 5 micron filter element in Viqua housing

Stage 2- Either use the Aquasana or Hahn (available Costco) HF-600 or HF-1000 GAC filter or AO Smith "Central GAC" from Lowes. {AO Smith owns Aquasana/Hahn}

Stage 3- 4 1/2" x 20" Nelson .35 (that's point 35) micron filter (even if it says washable / rinse able it is not) from Amazon in a Viqua housing

*That filters the entire house; just filtering out the Chlorine/Chloramides from your shower water is perhaps one of the most important health bangs for the buck you can get before you start getting to the point where you are removing fluoride from your drinking water.

Now for stage 4 (this only serves the kitchen faucet; faucet should be modern no lead / no leaded brass etc.)-

Alternative #1- 4 1/2" x 20" Activated Alumina cartridge from PureWaterSite.com in Viqua housing with optional follow on GAC filter in 2" X 10" or 4 1/2" x 10" or 4 1/2" x 20" with matching housing.

Alternative #2- Reverse osmosis with dedicated spigot (system comes with dedicated spigot) I'd suggest the Pro Q75 (AQTPROQ75) You can purchase this Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania RO system from plumbing supply houses. The replacement filters are available on Amazon.

Many will assert that you do not need nearly as large pre and post filters as I suggest. They are correct BUT- The larger filters move the water more slowly through any part of the filtering media. You want to move the water slowly through the filtering media; that lets is work the way it is intended. The suggested larger sizes also GREATLY reduce the frequency of filter changes. If you have a relatively modern municipal water supply system it is very possible (likely) that you will not have to do anything other than rinse the 5 micron pre filter once a year and not have to worry about the rest of the system for 4 years with a family of four.

I am not at all a water specialist. But I do know water filtration and delivery is much more complicated than what we are lead to believe. If you start to research it you will find that there is much argument over "structured water" and how filters kind of strip the fabric or essence of the water. There are arguments that you have to take the water as I've describe after filtration and place it in a container and chill to 54 degrees F for a couple of hours in order for the water to "heal." I just don't know about all that. Not everything in our water other than Hydrogen and Oxygen are bad for us. Many people add a dash of quality sea salt or real salt back into their filtered water to replace minerals stripped away during the filtering process.
